title: Prediction of high-flow nasal cannula failure in COVID-19 acute hypoxemic respiratory failure using combined clinical and metabolomic data: a machine learning study.
summary: A random-forest model combined clinical and metabolomic data to predict high-flow nasal cannula failure in a prospective COVID-19 cohort. A temporally independent cohort was also examined, but it included only 22 patients; this does not establish clinical utility.
ai_technology: Random-forest prediction using clinical and metabolomic features
organization: Hospital del Mar; Hospital del Mar Research Institute; Universitat Pompeu Fabra

evidence.tested: Prospective cohort evaluation and temporal validation were reported; the temporal cohort contained 22 patients.
evidence.unknown: The temporal sample is small, and prediction performance does not establish improved treatment decisions or patient outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest prediction using clinical and metabolomic features

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
